title: Widest Spread From Two Digit Rewrites
statement:
A rewrite of a positive integer num picks two digits x and y (they may be equal) and replaces every occurrence of x in num with y. The result must not start with 0 and must not be 0.

Make two independent rewrites of the original num, giving a and b. Return the largest possible value of a − b.

examples.why: Rewrite 5→9 for a = 999 and 5→1 for b = 111.
a = 9020 (1→9). For b the leading 1 is already as small as allowed, and turning 1 into 0 would create a leading zero, so rewrite 2→0: b = 1000.
a: the leading 9 cannot grow, so raise the next digit, 2→9: 9988. b: 9→1 gives 1288. Raising the smallest digit instead would not help: position beats value.

hints: The two rewrites are independent: make a as large as possible and b as small as possible.
For the maximum, the leftmost digit that is not 9 is the one worth turning into 9. For the minimum, think about the leading digit first.
Minimum: if the first digit is not 1, rewrite it to 1. If it is 1, rewrite the first digit that is neither 0 nor 1 to 0 (the 1s cannot become 0 without a leading zero).

explain.intuition:
Since a and b come from separate rewrites, maximize one and minimize the other. Higher positions dominate, so for a find the leftmost digit that is not already 9 and turn all copies of it into 9.

For b, the leading digit cannot become 0, so the best it can be is 1. If it is not 1, rewrite it to 1. If it already is 1, every 1 must stay (rewriting 1→0 would zero the leading digit), so look for the leftmost digit that is neither 0 nor 1 and send it to 0.
steps: a: find the first digit d ≠ 9; if found, replace every d with 9.
b: if s[0] ≠ 1, replace every s[0] with 1. Otherwise find the first digit not in {0, 1} and replace every copy with 0.
pitfalls: Replacing only the first occurrence of the digit. A rewrite changes every copy, as in 9288 where both 8s would change if 8 were chosen.
Rewriting 1→0 for the minimum when the number starts with 1, which creates a leading zero.
Picking the smallest digit to raise instead of the leftmost non-9 one. In 9288 the 2 matters more than any later digit because of its position.

solutions.title: Try all 100 rewrites
solutions.idea: Apply every (x, y) pair, keep the valid results, and subtract the smallest from the largest.

solutions.title: Greedy on the leftmost useful digit
solutions.idea: Max: leftmost non-9 becomes 9. Min: leading digit becomes 1, or if it is 1, the leftmost digit above 1 becomes 0.

followups: Each rewrite may change only one occurrence of a digit. How does the greedy change?
You must use the same x for both rewrites. Is the problem still greedy?
lcTitle: Max Difference You Can Get From Changing an Integer
